feedback: The RM faithfully encodes the composite task. Task reading: 'try not to do both' forbids the conjunction of the two listed events — dropping the key while the door is closed (key_lost) together with opening the door (door_open) — while still requiring the box pickup. Since the box room is reachable only through the door, door_open alone is necessary progress; the violation is completing the pair. The machine captures exactly this: u1 marks key_lost with a small -0.1, and the pair is completed either as (u1, door_open) -> u3 (-1.0) or as (u2, key_lost) -> u3 (-1.0, reachable because door_open can be toggled shut before the key is dropped), with u3 absorbing so a violating trajectory cannot bank the goal reward. The clean path (u0 -> u6 blocker_moved +0.1 -> u5 has_door_key +0.1 -> u2 door_open +0.2 -> u4 target_picked_up +1.0) mirrors the reference trace: ball moved first, key picked up second, door opened, key dropped after door_open (key_lost correctly does not fire when the door is open, since it requires !door_open), box picked up. Dropping the key inside the open room stays in u2 via the else self-loop with no penalty, which is correct. The ball-first ordering is strategically meaningful here (the key-first order forces a key drop behind the closed door), so the +0.1 blocker_moved progress reward is task-relevant, not spurious. Persistent/event distinctions are handled correctly: key_lost is used as a one-step trigger with a dedicated self-loop, persistent conditions (blocker_moved, has_door_key, door_open) gate the ordered guards, and blocker_moved regression (dropping the ball back) needs no explicit edge because it cannot affect the forbidden pair. All guards are predicate-only conjunctions of the five propositions; every state has an else self-loop covering irrelevant events; rewards are bounded in [-1.0, +1.0]; no reward can be farmed because each positive guard fires only on first entry to its target state and door re-opening after a shut toggle stays in u2 via else. Neither blemish changes behavior on reachable traces.

feedback:
All five environment-declared propositions are implemented; no undeclared extras, no missing predicates, no imports, no side effects, and syntactically valid read-only Python.

- blocker_moved: the scan tests, for every (x,y), whether a door sits at (x,y) with a ball at (x-1,y). With exactly one door at (dx,dy) and one ball this is exactly equivalent to the reference check 'no ball at (dx-1,dy)': it is False only when the ball is on the cell directly in front of the door on the start side, True when the ball is carried (off-grid, counts as moved), and False again if the ball is dropped back on that cell. Range bounds are safe (x starts at 1, door is never on the border).
- has_door_key and door_open match the reference grid-scan expressions exactly (guarding empty cells, matching key color to the door, is_open on the door).
- target_picked_up matches the reference mission check (carrying a box whose color matches 'pick up the <color> box').
- key_lost: correct event semantics. It reads env.episode_memory['previous_valuation'] read-only and fires on exactly one step when has_door_key was true at the previous step and both current has_door_key and door_open are false; false otherwise. The truthiness guard for the previous valuation is harmless: at the first step the valuation exists with has_door_key false, so the event is false there either way. By construction it never co-occurs with has_door_key, door_open, or target_picked_up, consistent with the reward machine constraints.

API usage is confined to documented reads (env.grid.get, env.carrying, env.mission, env.width, env.height, object type/color/is_open, previous_valuation); nothing mutates the environment or episode memory. Propositions compose correctly with the RM transitions (e.g., picking up the ball alone satisfies blocker_moved & !has_door_key & !door_open & !key_lost in u0).
